tags.gist: Summarizes four additions for agentic devices: an entity registration spine, evidence-gated state transitions, named silent failures and human-authorized capability expansion.
Says agentic deployment shifts what must be reviewed from a model's outputs to a configuration of entities that may change composition after clearance.
Would define an agentic device as registered, versioned, linked entities: the agent, its models, authorized tools and data sources, and qualification datasets.
Would have premarket submissions pin a frozen configuration graph of agent, model, data-source and dataset versions for review.
Would turn any postmarket departure from the registered graph, a new tool or swapped model, into a detectable, reportable event instead of invisible drift.
Says the spine makes explicit which entities the sponsor controls versus merely references, linking to master files without conflating device and foundation model.
Wants each registration event and configuration change to leave a hash-chained record, with the audit trail as the enforceable core.
Says no new legal authority is needed; it reuses identification, versioning and supplier controls, which the paper's element set touches only via A.1.
Proposes change control as evidence-gated state transitions: a lifecycle-affecting change may occur only once the evidence the sponsor declared for it exists.
Illustrates evidence per transition type: benchmarks for activation, manifest and re-run for model updates, provenance for tool changes, re-verification before return to service.
Wants an unmet requirement to block the transition with a denial receipt, and a paused device to resume only via a fresh evidence-carrying transition.
Says the state-transition frame carries the premarket evidentiary logic forward to each later configuration change, giving both halves one spine.
Wants FDA to name silent failure patterns explicitly: failure modes with no error signal that pass conventional performance dashboards.
Wants input-distribution drift tracked as a first-class signal, since aggregate accuracy can hold while a shifted subpopulation degrades.
Wants staleness of tools, databases or datasets outside their validity window monitored as a lifecycle event rather than found at the next review.
Wants observed agent action trajectories compared against the declared operating envelope, since agents can finish tasks by paths nobody evaluated.
Would govern the response to each silent failure as a transition, pause, roll back, re-verify, resume through the gate, and list the patterns in guidance.
Proposes a bright-line rule: an agentic device cannot reach a higher-impact capability tier except by an explicit, evidence-carrying human authorization.
Would keep technical capability distinct from standing authorization, so invoking an unpermitted function requires an authorization transition.
Would declare permission tiers at design time, from read-only retrieval to direct clinical influence, with the highest default-denied and human-granted.
Keeps machine requests and human decisions at the points where consequences step up in kind, each tier crossing leaving an auditable receipt.
Says the four recommendations reuse machinery industry already runs and were prototyped as a small state machine, so they are practical.
Thanks FDA and hopes the agentic portion of the framework develops along lifecycle-complete lines.
